hints.title: What disproves every?
hints.body: The statement claims a strict inequality for every real pair. To show it false, one allowed pair where the strict inequality fails is enough.
hints.recap: A universal statement is defeated by one counterexample.
hints.pitfall: You do not need to list all failing pairs.

recall.reminder: One permitted failure disproves a for-all claim.

hints.title: Check the offered calculation
hints.body: Substitute the proposed values into both sides of the exact inequality, retaining its strict inequality sign.
hints.recap: The strict and non-strict comparisons have different equality cases.
hints.pitfall: Use the statement printed in the question rather than a familiar replacement theorem.
hints.pause: Determine whether the offered pair makes the original inequality true.

recall.reminder: The strict and non-strict comparisons have different equality cases.

hints.title: Match the proof to its goal
hints.body: Check separately that the proposed pair belongs to the domain and that the logical conclusion follows from its comparison.
hints.recap: A disproof of a universal claim does not require a replacement theorem.
hints.pitfall: Do not assume that a correctly calculated example automatically has the needed logical role.
hints.pause: Assess both the claim and the validity of the student’s disproof before choosing an option.

recall.reminder: A disproof of a universal claim does not require a replacement theorem.

solution:
The pair a=3, b=4 belongs to the stated real domain. It gives |a+b|=7 and |a|+|b|=7, so the proposed strict inequality becomes 7<7, which is false.

A single allowed counterexample disproves a statement asserted for all pairs. There is no requirement to find every counterexample or to state a corrected theorem.

The claim is false and the student’s proof is fully correct: E.
knowledgePattern: Validate one counterexample to a universal strict inequality
